doc.name: A — candles catalogue, retail shelf, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: three-wick soy candle
Category: candles
Shot programme: retail shelf
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You run the tabletop stage for a premium candles product shoot. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the floating levitation in a retail shelf treatment.

SUBJECT. A three-wick soy candle. Copy the product from the reference verbatim in form and finish. If a detail is unreadable in the reference, keep it neutral rather than inventing one.

CAMERA. Product suspended mid-air with no visible support and a soft drop shadow beneath. Shoot on a 24mm wide at f/1.4, framing for leading lines converging on the subject from the lower corners.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with a hard fresnel through an egg-crate grid for a crisp-edged shadow. Stage the product on or against oiled walnut, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a sun-bleached grade with faded blacks and a green-yellow bias. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Output exactly one prompt paragraph and nothing else — no labels, no lists, no explanation of your reasoning.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.

CAMERA. Cap off, lid open or mechanism deployed, mid-use state. Shoot on a probe macro lens at f/11, framing for dead-centre symmetry with mirrored negative space.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with underlighting from a translucent base panel. Stage the product on or against cast pigmented resin, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward near-monochrome with a single accent hue allowed to stay saturated. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. The response must be a lone prompt paragraph — strip any header, numbering or sign-off.
